docs.html:
1Purpose

This policy sets out what [Provider name] commits to when we provide . It is for whose situation carries high risk or complexity, their families and advocates, our , and the people who check our work.

2Applies to

  • Every participant who receives specialised support coordination from [Provider name], and every person who asks us for it, before they sign (the Registration Rules, Schedule 6, clause 1(2)(a)).
  • Everyone who works for us on that support: employees, contractors, agency workers, volunteers and key personnel.
  • The whole of the coordination: assessing , planning for a , finding and briefing , monitoring, and reporting.
  • Any other support we or anyone connected with us provide to the same participant. Commitment 13 keeps it separate from the coordination.

Short names used here:

  • "The Registration Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Provider Registration and Practice Standards) Rules 2018.
  • "The Incident Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Incident Management and Reportable Incidents) Rules 2018.
  • "The Code" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Code of Conduct) Rules 2018, section 6.

3Commitments

C1

We will allocate each participant a coordinator who is qualified, trained and signed off as competent for that participant's risks and complexity. A coordinator holds [qualification and years of experience we require]. The expects specialised support coordination to be delivered by a qualified and experienced practitioner, such as a social worker, psychologist, occupational therapist or mental health nurse, or a person with equivalent demonstrated experience in complex situations; set the requirement at adoption with that in mind. They have completed our training on the risk factors listed in FRM-SCO-01 . They have supervision with the Service Manager at least every month.

Because the law says: ←Legislation, point (1)Legislation (1)How we do it: →Procedure, step 1Procedure step 1

C2

We will assess each participant's risks and complexity with them. We use their own account and the risk factors and rating scale in FRM-SCO-01 Risk and Crisis Response Plan. At the first meeting we agree interim safety steps and set a provisional risk level. We make the plan within the time for that level in PRO-SCO-02 Decision table 2, counted from the first meeting: 5 for extreme risk, 10 for high, 15 for medium and low. A second person, the , reads and challenges the assessment and plan: before the plan is issued for a participant at high or extreme risk, and within 10 business days of issue for every other participant.

Because the law says: ←Legislation, point (1)Legislation (1)←Legislation, point (2)Legislation (2)How we do it: →Procedure, step 7Procedure step 7→Procedure, step 8Procedure step 8→Procedure, step 11Procedure step 11

C3

We will make a Risk and Crisis Response Plan with each participant, in their words and in a form they can use. It names their warning signs, what helps, and who does what if a crisis or a happens. We give the participant their copy. We review the plan at the interval for their risk level, and after any crisis, incident or major change.

Because the law says: ←Legislation, point (2)Legislation (2)How we do it: →Procedure, step 3Procedure step 3→Procedure, step 9Procedure step 9→Procedure, step 10Procedure step 10→Procedure, step 12Procedure step 12→Procedure, step 29Procedure step 29

C4

We will always have someone who has read the participant's plan and can respond to a crisis. That is the coordinator, or the when the coordinator is away. In our hours a coordinator or cover who has read the plan answers a crisis call and starts the plan within 2 hours. Outside our hours the participant's plan names who they call, and we say truthfully whether that is us.

Because the law says: ←Legislation, point (2)Legislation (2)How we do it: →Procedure, step 1Procedure step 1→Procedure, step 4Procedure step 4→Procedure, step 25Procedure step 25→Procedure, step 26Procedure step 26→Procedure, step 27Procedure step 27→Procedure, step 28Procedure step 28

C5

We will consult the participant when we plan and coordinate supports, and before each plan review. With their consent, we also consult their and . We record who the participant agreed we may talk to and what we may tell them. We respect a refusal.

Because the law says: ←Legislation, point (3)Legislation (3)How we do it: →Procedure, step 5Procedure step 5→Procedure, step 7Procedure step 7→Procedure, step 13Procedure step 13

C6

We will identify suitable providers for each support. We check registration where it applies, evidence of skills and experience for the participant's kind of situation, and fit with their preferences. We follow one options rule, set in POL-SCO-02 C4: at least three suitable options able to meet the need, of which at least two have no relationship to us, where that many exist, and we say which have a relationship to us. Where fewer exist we record who we asked and tell the participant why.

Because the law says: ←Legislation, point (4)Legislation (4)How we do it: →Procedure, step 15Procedure step 15→Procedure, step 16Procedure step 16

C7

We will make sure every provider who carries out the plan understands the participant's risks and their own part before their first support. We brief each provider on the parts of the plan the participant agreed to share. We get their confirmation in writing.

Because the law says: ←Legislation, point (5)Legislation (5)How we do it: →Procedure, step 18Procedure step 18→Procedure, step 19Procedure step 19

C8

We will bring the participant's providers and other services together to work as one team. We hold a coordination meeting at the interval for the participant's risk level. We hold another within 5 business days after any crisis, incident or breakdown of supports. Every action has an owner and a date.

Because the law says: ←Legislation, point (5)Legislation (5)How we do it: →Procedure, step 20Procedure step 20→Procedure, step 29Procedure step 29

C9

We will monitor each participant's plan. We contact the participant at the interval for their risk level and check that each support is delivered as planned. When a support is not delivered as planned we act within 5 business days.

Because the law says: ←Legislation, point (6)Legislation (6)How we do it: →Procedure, step 21Procedure step 21

C10

We will check each participant's plan budget and plan dates every month, in the first 5 business days of the month. For each funding category we compare the share used and booked with the share of plan time elapsed. A gap of more than 15 percentage points is explained, and the participant is told within 5 business days, and their plan manager too if they have one. This is the same monthly funds check as POL-SCO-02 C11. It is done once, under PRO-SCO-02 step 22, and recorded on FRM-SCO-02 Section H. When a plan is within 12 weeks of its reassessment date and no review has been scheduled, we ask the NDIA to confirm one.

Because the law says: ←Legislation, point (6)Legislation (6)How we do it: →Procedure, step 22Procedure step 22

C11

We will meet every reporting obligation attached to the participant's plan. We list each report and notice owed when coordination starts: the NDIA's implementation report, due 8 weeks after coordination starts; mid-term reports at the frequency the request for service sets; and the plan reassessment report before the plan review, which we draft with the participant 8 weeks before the reassessment date and send 6 weeks before it, or by the date the NDIA sets. Due dates come from the request for service and the provider portal. We show the participant each report about them before we send it. We send it by its due date, or tell the recipient before the date passes if we will miss it.

Because the law says: ←Legislation, point (6)Legislation (6)How we do it: →Procedure, step 6Procedure step 6→Procedure, step 23Procedure step 23→Procedure, step 24Procedure step 24

C12

We will arrange supports as the participant directs, using their plan funds for the purposes they intend. We give them their options in the language and form they understand, and build their skills to manage their own supports if they wish. POL-SCO-02 Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Policy sets this out.

How we do it: →Procedure, step 17Procedure step 17

C13

We will keep specialised support coordination separate from any other support we, or anyone connected with us, provide. We give each participant our conflict of policy and its plain summary in the format they use, and check they can say back what it means. We explain, and check they can say back, how coordination differs from the other supports in their plan. We take no payment, gift or benefit for naming or referring a provider. We tell the participant about any interest we hold before they choose, and their choice of provider never changes their coordination. We record every referral to or from another provider in REG-SCO-02 Support Coordination Referral Register. PRO-SCO-01 Support Coordination Conflict of Interest Procedure sets how.

How we do it: →Procedure, step 14Procedure step 14→Procedure, step 16Procedure step 16

C14

We will not leave a participant without a plan when coordination ends or changes. Before our last day we hand the Risk and Crisis Response Plan to the next coordinator, with the participant's consent. We also give the participant their copy.

How we do it: →Procedure, step 30Procedure step 30

4Ground rules

G1

The participant leads. Their words, their choices and their pace come first. We never decide for a participant who can decide for themselves.

G2

We share a participant's information only with the people they have agreed to. The exceptions are a call to 000, a legal duty, and a serious threat to life, health or safety when we cannot ask first. We tell the participant at the start that these exceptions exist, and tell them if we use one.

G3

A coordinator is not a clinician or a behaviour support practitioner. We pass health and behaviour questions to the participant's practitioner. We never write a restrictive practice into a plan. Only an authorised behaviour support plan can hold one. PRO-BSP-02 Regulated Restrictive Practices Procedure applies if someone asks.

G4

A participant who says no has made a decision. We record it, ask again at the next review, and never end coordination because of it.

G5

We say our hours truthfully. We do not suggest we are a crisis service unless we staff one. The participant's plan says who they call outside our hours.

G6

Nobody at [Provider name] can extend a time limit that the law sets.

G7

A participant at high or extreme risk never goes without interim safety steps, a cover coordinator and a named person to call.

G8

A concern about a coordinator goes to the Service Manager. A concern about the Service Manager goes to the Chief Executive. A concern about the Chief Executive goes to the chair of the governing body. In a provider with one owner it goes to the . Anyone can also phone the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544.

G9

In a small provider one person may hold several roles. A sole trader holds every role except the case reviewer, who is a person outside the business. The cover coordinator may be a coordinator from another provider, engaged in writing. The independent contact for concerns may be the case reviewer. The case reviewer also gives the sole trader supervision at least every month, reads the register as REG-SCO-01 sets out, and does the checks in "How we check" that would otherwise be the sole trader checking their own work. The sole trader engages the case reviewer and any outside cover in writing, with a confidentiality undertaking and agreed response times, names them on adoption and tells each participant who they are.

G10

The system does not depend on any one software product. Paper works when systems are down.

G11

Every participant is told how to complain, and how to change their coordinator or a provider. We tell them at the first meeting and at each plan review. POL-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Policy sets how we handle a complaint.

  • The same Module, sections 65 and 66 and Schedule 6, clauses 4 and 5, which POL-SCO-02 and PRO-SCO-01 answer in full. POL-SCO-02 is the controlled policy for clause 4; commitment 12 is a pointer to it. Commitment 13 carries the clause 5 commitments, and PRO-SCO-01 sets the steps.

  • The Registration Rules, section 7: the classes of supports that need a registered provider.

  • NDIS Act 2013, section 73ZDA: the NDIS Provider Register, which lists registered providers, their classes of supports, conditions and suspensions, and banning orders.
  • NDIS Act 2013, sections 73F(2)(b), (c), (g) and (h) and 73J. Complying with the Code, the Practice Standards and the incident rules is a condition of registration.
  • The Code, section 6(1)(a) to (g). It covers respect for self-determination, privacy, safe and competent supports, integrity, raising concerns, and preventing violence, abuse, neglect, exploitation and sexual misconduct.
  • The Incident Rules: Part 2, sections 9, 10 and 12, and Part 3, sections 19, 20, 21 and 25.
  • National Disability Insurance Scheme (Approved Quality Auditors Scheme) Guidelines 2018, Annex B, items B.2 and B.3. Specialised support coordination is a high risk group for audit sampling. Participants are in the sample unless they opt out.
  • The NDIS Pricing Arrangements and Price Limits, for the conditions and price limits that apply to specialised support coordination.
  • Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), where it applies to us, and the privacy and health records law of [state or territory].
  • The child protection, guardianship, mental health and criminal law of [state or territory].
  • Law changing: from 20 November 2026 a new section 73VA of the NDIS Act 2013 makes it an offence and a civil penalty for an NDIS provider to give or offer any gift or benefit likely to induce a person to use its services. It comes from Act No. 66, 2026, Schedule 2, Part 8. Our rule in commitment 13 is wider and already covers it. Review commitment 13 and PRO-SCO-02 step 14 before that date.

9Words we use

471 words
specialised support coordination
help for a participant whose situation carries high risk or complexity. It means putting their NDIS plan into action, monitoring it and reviewing it, and reducing the risk and complexity of their situation.
participant
a person with disability who receives specialised support coordination from us, or who is asking us for it.
NDIS plan
the plan the NDIA approves for the participant, with its funding and dates.
NDIA
the National Disability Insurance Agency, which runs the NDIS and approves NDIS plans. The Quality Indicators call it "the Agency".
coordinator
the worker who does the coordination with a participant.
cover coordinator
a second coordinator, with the same sign-off, who acts when the coordinator is away. For a sole trader this may be a coordinator from another provider, engaged in writing.
case reviewer
a person who reads the assessment and plan for each participant, and challenges them. They are not the coordinator for that participant. For a sole trader the case reviewer is a person outside the business.
Risk and Crisis Response Plan
the plan we make with the participant in FRM-SCO-01. It holds their risks, warning signs, what helps and the steps to take in a crisis.
risk and complexity
the things in a participant's life that could seriously harm them or others. It also means anything that makes their supports hard to arrange or keep steady.
crisis
a point where someone is at risk of serious harm, or where supports the participant depends on have broken down or are about to.
breakdown of supports
a support the participant relies on stops, or is not delivered as planned, and the participant is at risk or worse off.
critical support
a support that would put the participant at risk if it stopped, named in FRM-SCO-01 Risk and Crisis Response Plan.
provider
an NDIS provider, registered or not, who gives a support in the participant's NDIS plan.
mainstream service
a service for the whole community, such as health, housing, justice, child safety, mental health, education or transport.
support network
the people in the participant's life whom they choose to involve, such as family, friends, carers and advocates.
independent advocate

1Purpose

The result: every who receives has their risks understood, and a plan they helped make. Their understand and act on that plan. The plan is monitored and reported on until it ends.

This procedure gives effect to POL-SCO-01 Specialised Support Coordination Policy, C1 to C14.

Short names used here:

  • "The Incident Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Incident Management and Reportable Incidents) Rules 2018.
  • "The Registration Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Provider Registration and Practice Standards) Rules 2018.
  • "The Code" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Code of Conduct) Rules 2018, section 6.
  • "The " means the National Disability Insurance Agency. The Quality Indicators call it "the Agency".

2When and who

Start this procedure when:

  • a participant, or their , agrees to start specialised support coordination (steps 1 to 19)
  • you learn of a crisis, an incident or a (steps 25 to 28)
  • a contact, a meeting, a budget check or a report falls due (steps 20 to 24)
  • a review date arrives, or a trigger in Decision table 4 happens (step 29)
  • coordination is about to end, or the is about to change for good (step 30).

A crisis is a point where someone is at risk of serious harm. It is also a point where supports the participant depends on have broken down or are about to.

Who acts:

  • The coordinator does the work with the participant. Each participant has one named coordinator.
  • The acts when the coordinator is away. They read each plan within 2 of issue, the same day for a participant at extreme risk.
  • The Service Manager names the coordinator and the cover coordinator, takes same-day calls, reads the register every month and approves each closing.
  • The reads the assessment and plan for each participant and challenges them: before the plan is issued for a participant at high or extreme risk, and within 10 business days of issue otherwise. The Service Manager is the case reviewer, unless they are also the coordinator for that participant. Then an outside person is the case reviewer.
  • The Quality Manager checks that the register is kept and acts on trends.
  • The Chief Executive takes concerns about managers.
  • Whoever takes a crisis call may be any of these people. Outside our hours it is whoever Q27 of the participant's plan names. That can be a crisis service and not us.

In a small provider one person may hold several of these roles. REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register shows who holds each.

If you are a sole trader, or the one director of a company:

  • You hold every role except the case reviewer. The case reviewer is a person outside the business, engaged in writing with a confidentiality undertaking and agreed response times (a draft plan read within 2 business days of receiving it). They also give you supervision at least every month and do the register reads that REG-SCO-01 sets for the case reviewer. The , named in REG-GOV-01, takes concerns about you; this may be the same person as the case reviewer.
  • Your cover coordinator may be a coordinator from another provider, engaged in writing. They read each plan within 2 business days of issue, the same day for a participant at extreme risk. You name the case reviewer and the cover before your first participant, and tell each participant who they are and what they may be told.
  • Where a step says to tell the Service Manager, write the date and time. For a participant at high or extreme risk, also tell the case reviewer the same day. A concern about you goes to the independent contact for concerns.

3Before you start

  • The participant, or their decision maker, has agreed to start. You have AGR-SUP-01 Service Agreement Template signed, or an interim written agreement, and the participant's .
  • The plan includes specialised support coordination funding.
  • You have the participant's communication preferences (FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form), or a blank copy.
  • You have a blank FRM-SCO-01 and can open REG-SCO-01 Support Coordination Register.
  • You have completed training on the risk factors at FRM-SCO-01 Q11 and on this procedure. REG-HRM-02 Training and Competency Register shows you are signed off as competent for specialised support coordination.
  • You know who your cover coordinator and case reviewer are.
  • You have the numbers for 000, for the crisis service for [state or territory], and for the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544. The Commission line is not an emergency line.

Before first use, the Chief Executive fills every square bracket in the four coordination documents, except [Provider name]. The Quality Manager checks that none is left blank. These are the decisions:

  • the qualification and years of experience a coordinator needs (POL-SCO-01 C1)
  • our hours, and what we tell a participant about outside them (FRM-SCO-01 Q27)
  • the crisis service for [state or territory] (FRM-SCO-01 Q26)
  • the child protection reporting rule for [state or territory] (FRM-SCO-01 Q31)
  • for a sole trader, the case reviewer, the cover coordinator and the independent contact for concerns
  • the name of the system that holds REG-SCO-01, and where paper copies are kept
  • who takes a privacy complaint (FRM-SCO-01 Privacy).

Before adoption, walk these scenarios through with two coordinators and the case reviewer, or, for a sole trader, with the case reviewer and the cover coordinator. Record it under "Reviewed with":

  • a participant who is evicted tomorrow and has nobody to call
  • a night call from a participant who says they want to die
  • a provider who withdraws on a Friday afternoon
  • a family member who asks for the plan after the participant said no
  • a plan that ends in 3 weeks with no review date.

4Watch out

  • Call 000 first. Call before anything else when a person is in danger now. A delay in a crisis can cost a life.
  • A crisis plan nobody has read does not work. A cover coordinator or provider who has not read it cannot act at 2 am, and may make things worse.
  • You are not a clinician. Health or behaviour advice you are not trained to give can harm the participant. Ask their practitioner and write what they say.
  • A plan we write never holds a restrictive practice. Holding, locking in, withholding things or a medicine to calm, written into a plan, can harm the participant and break the law. Only an authorised behaviour support plan can hold one.
  • Never share beyond what the participant agreed. A plan shared with the wrong person can put the participant in danger, most of all where the concern is someone close to them.
  • Do not promise secrecy. You may have to act to keep someone safe. A promise you cannot keep breaks trust.
  • Payment or a gift for naming a provider breaks the Code. It puts our advice in doubt and can lead to action by the NDIS Commission (the Code, section 6(1)(d)).
  • A plan whose reassessment date passes with no review scheduled leaves the participant unsure of their funding. The plan stays in effect until the NDIA makes a new one, but a late review can leave a gap between what the plan funds and what the participant now needs. Check the dates every month and ask the NDIA 12 weeks out.
  • A missed report date can weaken the participant's plan review. The NDIA may decide without our evidence.
  • The concern may be about a colleague or a manager. A report that goes only to the person it is about can be buried. "If it goes wrong" gives another line.
  • A participant's refusal is a decision. Record it, respect it and ask again at the next review. Do not end coordination because of it.

5Steps

Start

Step 1

The Service Manager

Name the coordinator and the cover coordinator.

Choose a coordinator who meets the position description (FRM-HRM-03 Position Description Template). REG-HRM-02 must show them signed off as competent and trained in the risk factors at FRM-SCO-01 Q11. Do not give a participant to a coordinator whose skills do not fit their risks. Allocate on the complexity the referral describes, and re-check the coordinator's caseload against the contact interval in Decision table 2 when the level is set at step 8. Name a second person with the same sign-off as cover; for a sole trader this may be a coordinator from another provider, engaged in writing. Tell the participant both names at the first meeting.

Result
Each participant has a coordinator who is competent for their risks, and a cover who can act.
Record

Step 2

The coordinator

Open the participant's row.

Enter the row number, the participant's NDIS participant number (the name stays on FRM-SCO-01 and the participant's file), the date they agreed to start and the date of the first meeting. Enter the plan start and end dates, and the reassessment date if the NDIA has set one. Enter who manages the funds, and the coordination funding and hours. Check the plan has enough funding to last to its end date. If not, tell the participant and the Service Manager the same day, and follow step 22.

Result

Record

Step 3

The coordinator

Ask how the participant wants to take part.

Ask where and when they want to meet, how long, how they like to communicate and who they want with them. Use the supports in their communication preferences. Book an interpreter or communication support if they need one. Offer an now, and again when the plan is agreed. Ask whether anyone else has legal authority to decide for them, and ask to see the document. A decision maker decides only what their authority covers. Tell the participant they can ask to change their coordinator or a provider at any time, and how to complain.

Result
The participant leads how their plan is made, and we know who may decide for them.

Step 4

The coordinator

Ask the three safety questions and agree interim steps.

Ask: is anyone in danger right now? What could stop or go wrong in the next 4 weeks? Who should we call first if something does? Write each answer in the participant's words. Agree what you and they will do if it happens before the plan is finished. If anyone is in danger now, go to step 25 first. From the answers, set a provisional risk level with Decision table 1 and write it at Q15 as provisional; the plan clock in Decision table 2 starts today. Give the participant your number, our hours and who to call outside them.

The participant is safe enough to wait for the plan, and knows who to call.

Ask who we may talk to, which parts they may be told and until when. Think of family, carers, current providers, health practitioners, housing, justice, child safety and the NDIA. The coordinator

List every report and notice we owe.

Read the NDIS plan, the service agreement, the request for service and any written request from the NDIA, the plan manager or another funder. The NDIA's reports are: the implementation report, due 8 weeks after coordination starts; mid-term reports at the frequency the request for service sets; and the plan reassessment report before the plan review, which we draft with the participant 8 weeks before the reassessment date and send 6 weeks before it, or by the date the NDIA sets (steps 23 and 24). Take due dates from the request for service and the provider portal. Add any date the participant tells you matters, such as a tribunal or a housing review. Update the list whenever the plan changes.

Every duty has a due date and a source before supports start.

Step 7

The coordinator

Learn the participant's situation, their words first.

Ask the participant what is hardest now and what they want to change. Write what they say. Then, with their consent from step 5, read the NDIS plan, earlier assessments and reports, and the incident and crisis history. List the supports in place now. Talk only to the people they agreed. Write each conversation in col W. Link to another provider's clinical content. Do not copy it into our plan.

The participant's account comes first, and the facts support it.

The coordinator

Assess the participant's risks and complexity with them.

Go through each factor in the hint at Q11. For each that applies, write what has happened, what the participant thinks, and a rating on the scale printed at Q12: low, medium, high or extreme. Ask what they want done and which risks they accept. Explain the risk and the options first. For a risk rated high or extreme that they accept, complete FRM-RGT-04 Dignity of Risk Decision Record. Ask who else could be harmed. Set the overall level with Decision table 1. A final level higher than the provisional one set at step 4 shortens the remaining time in Decision table 2; a lower one never lengthens it. Tell the Service Manager the same day if the level is high or extreme, and re-check the caseload (step 1).

Each risk is named, rated and discussed, and the participant has an overall level.

Make the plan

Step 9

The coordinator

Write the warning signs and what helps, in the participant's words.

Ask what they notice in themselves when things start to go wrong. Ask what family, workers and other providers notice, and write who said it. Ask what makes things worse, what helps and what must not be done. Ask for the first sign, not the last. Never write a restraint, a lock, a withheld item or a medicine to calm. Only an authorised behaviour support plan can hold one, and PRO-BSP-02 Regulated Restrictive Practices Procedure applies if someone asks for it.

In Section D, list the supports and people who keep things steady. Mark each support that would put the participant at risk if it stopped, and how long it can be missed. Agree actions that stop a crisis, each with an owner and a date. In Section E, say what counts as a crisis, the first steps for each kind, and the call list in order. State our hours truthfully. Say where the health information is kept, where the participant will go if home is not safe, and what they want in an emergency. Do not write a dose or a clinical step. Link to the practitioner's plan. Check the plan does not conflict with any behaviour support plan, health plan or court order the participant has.

A coordinator, a cover coordinator or a provider can act from this plan at 2 am.

Read the assessment and the draft plan, and challenge them.

Check the plan against the participant's own words. Check each factor has a rating and an action. Check the crisis steps work at 2 am, and each call-list number is complete. Check nothing restrictive is written in, and nothing conflicts with a behaviour support plan or health plan. Check the sharing list matches what the participant agreed. Write the changes you ask for. The participant has a plan that is theirs, in a form they can use, and our cover can act on it.

The coordinator

Consult the participant's and .

Ask the participant first, and tell them what each person said. With the consent from step 5, ask each person and agency what they see and what they can do. Check whether we hold an in any provider before naming it.

An interest is ownership, a shared owner or director, a family tie, a referral arrangement, or any payment, gift or benefit from a provider. If we hold one, stop. Follow PRO-SCO-01 Support Coordination Conflict of Interest Procedure before naming that provider. It uses FRM-SCO-03 Support Coordination Conflict of Interest Disclosure Record. Take nothing from a provider for naming or referring a participant. Tell the Service Manager the same day if anything is offered.

Every provider we name is named on merit, and any interest is declared to the participant.

Find suitable providers and check each one.

Use Decision table 3. For each support the plan needs, follow the options rule in POL-SCO-02 C4: find at least three suitable options where that many exist, at least two of them with no relationship to us, and say which have one. Check registration on the NDIS Provider Register. Ask for evidence of skills and experience with people in a similar situation, such as examples, team qualifications and referees the participant agrees to. Check availability, place, cost and fit with the participant's language, culture and preferences. Ask who they already know and trust. Write what you asked and what you got. Do not recommend a provider you could not check.

Every option put to the participant is checked, and the checks are on record.

Record who you asked and what they said.

List each provider you contacted, the date and the answer. Say why the others were not suitable. Tell the participant there are fewer choices, and why. Ask whether they want to wait or go ahead. If the only option is one of ours, follow PRO-SCO-01 and tell the Service Manager the same day.

Ask each provider to say in their own words what they will watch for and do. Get their confirmation in writing. An email is enough. Get the name and number of their contact in a crisis. Hold a coordination meeting with the participant and their providers.

Ask the participant who they want at the meeting and how it should run. With their consent, invite their providers and any mainstream service involved. Cover how supports are going and any crisis or near miss since the last meeting. Cover the warning signs seen, what is not working and who does what next. Write each action with an owner and a date. Send the actions to everyone who attended within 2 business days. If a provider misses two meetings in a row, tell the Service Manager.

Result
The providers work as one team, and every action has an owner and a date.
Record
REG-SCO-01 col AB
Time limit
First meeting within 20 business days of the first support starting. Then at the interval in Decision table 2, and within 5 business days of any crisis, incident or breakdown (our standard)

Monitor and report

Step 21

The coordinator, or the cover coordinator when the coordinator is away

Check in with the participant, and ask how each support is going.

Contact them at the interval in Decision table 2, in the way they chose at Q37. Ask how they are, how each support is going, what has changed and what worries them. Ask whether the supports are helping them towards the goals in their NDIS plan. Check each critical support first. Ask the provider when the participant reports a problem or a support was missed. When a support is not delivered as planned, act within 5 business days. Talk to the provider, adjust the support, or go to step 26 if it is a breakdown. If you cannot reach a participant at high or extreme risk, follow "If it goes wrong". Where Q14 names a risk to workers, tell the Service Manager when and where you visit, and check in with them after.

Result
We know how supports are going, and the participant has been heard.
Record
REG-SCO-01 col AC; REG-SCO-01 col AD
Time limit
At the interval in Decision table 2 (our standard)

Puts into action: ←Policy, commitment 9Policy C9Goes into: →Register, Contact with the participantRegister col AC→Register, Delivery checksRegister col AD

Step 22

The coordinator

Run the monthly plan check on the budget and the dates.

Run the one monthly funds check, on a new copy of FRM-SCO-02 Section H. For each funding category, compare the share used and booked with the share of the plan time that has passed. If the two differ by more than 15 percentage points (our standard), find out why. Tell the participant within 5 business days, and the plan manager if there is one. Check the coordination funding and hours. Check the provider portal for the due dates of the NDIA's reports. If the plan is within 12 weeks of its reassessment date and no review has been scheduled, ask the NDIA in writing to confirm the date. Do this with the participant's agreement. If you cannot see the budget, ask the participant, the plan manager or the NDIA, with the participant's consent. Update the dates in col F to col J, and the next report date in col AI. PRO-SCO-03 steps 26 and 27 set what the participant may choose to do about a gap.

Result
No budget surprise and no missed date.
Record
FRM-SCO-02 Q32 to Q35; REG-SCO-01 col AF (date and flags); REG-SCO-01 col AI
Time limit
In the first 5 business days of each month (our standard)

Step 23

The coordinator

Prepare the plan review report with the participant.

Start 12 weeks before the plan reassessment date (the plan end date where none is set). For a plan shorter than 12 weeks, start at its first meeting. This is the one plan review preparation for the participant; PRO-SCO-03 step 30 points here. Ask the participant what has worked, what has not and what they want next. Use the consultations, delivery checks, funds checks and events in the register. Say what changed in their risks, which supports worked and what is needed next, and why. Say plainly if different funding is needed and what happens without it. Show the participant the whole draft, in their format, with a plain summary of how their funds were used. They may add their own words or ask us to leave something out. Record what they asked. For a participant at high or extreme risk, the case reviewer reads it.

Result
A report that says what the participant wants, backed by our records.
Record
REG-SCO-01 col AH

Draft and plain summary to the participant at least 8 weeks before the plan reassessment date, and never later than the date the NDIA sets (our standard)

Step 24

The coordinator

Send each report by its due date.

Send each report listed in col AG, using the channel the NDIA or funder names. Send the plan review report only with the participant's agreement. Check it was received. Keep a copy. Send a participant's information to a funder only as far as the participant agreed, or the law requires. If a due date will be missed, tell the recipient before it passes, give a new date, and tell the Service Manager the same day.

Result
Every report is received on time, and the participant has seen it.
Record
REG-SCO-01 col AH
Time limit
By the due date the NDIA or funder sets. Where none is set, 6 weeks before the plan reassessment date for the plan reassessment report, and 8 weeks after coordination starts for the implementation report (our standard)

When something goes wrong

Step 25

Whoever takes the call or sees the danger

If someone is in danger now:

Call 000.

Call when a person is hurt, unconscious or not breathing, or has taken too much of something. Call when they say they are about to end their life or harm someone. If you are not sure, call 000. Say what has happened and where the person is. Stay on the line and follow the operator. Tell the crew what the plan says at Q28: the participant's conditions, allergies, that they take medicines and where the list is held, and how they communicate. Do not read out doses. If you are with the participant, stay with them. If you are not, stay on the phone with them until help arrives if you can, and ask someone nearby to stay. If they speak of wanting to die but are not about to act, stay with them, call the crisis service at Q26 and follow the plan. Then go to step 26.

Result
Emergency help is coming and the participant is not alone.
Record
REG-SCO-01 col AE
Time limit
Straight away (our standard)

Puts into action: ←Policy, commitment 4Policy C4Goes into: →Register, Crisis, incident or breakdown eventsRegister col AE

Step 26

The coordinator, the cover coordinator, or the person at the top of the call list

Follow the participant's plan for this kind of crisis.

Open the plan. Find the kind of crisis at Q25 and do the first steps. Phone the people at Q26, in order, until someone takes responsibility. Share only what the participant agreed. The exceptions are a call to 000, a duty in law, and a serious threat to life, health or safety when you cannot ask first. If a provider has not arrived or has withdrawn, phone them. Then phone the next choice at Q32 and tell the participant. Stay in contact until the crisis is settled or someone they trust has taken over. Write the times as you go. Do not give clinical advice. Connect them with a health professional or the crisis service.

Result
The participant is safe, and the right people know what is happening.
Record
REG-SCO-01 col AE
Time limit
Within 2 hours in business hours. Outside them, as Q27 says (our standard)

Puts into action: ←Policy, commitment 4Policy C4Goes into: →Register, Crisis, incident or breakdown eventsRegister col AE

Step 27

The coordinator

Tell the Service Manager.

Phone them. Say what happened, how the participant is, what you have done and which providers are involved. For a death, a serious injury or an allegation of abuse, phone at any hour. If the concern is about the Service Manager, phone the Chief Executive. In a provider with one owner, phone the independent contact for concerns. The Service Manager offers you a debrief within 5 business days.

Result
A manager knows, and can help the participant and the coordinator.
Record
REG-SCO-01 col AE
Time limit
Straight away for a death, a serious injury or an allegation of abuse. Otherwise the same day (our standard)

Puts into action: ←Policy, commitment 4Policy C4Goes into: →Register, Crisis, incident or breakdown eventsRegister col AE

Step 28

The coordinator

If the event is, or may be, an incident in connection with our supports, or you cannot tell:

Raise an incident report.

Use FRM-INC-01 Incident Report Form and follow PRO-INC-01 Incident Management Procedure. An incident in connection with our supports includes harm during our contact. It includes something we did or did not do, and an allegation about one of our workers. Raise it whenever we learn of it, whether or not another provider also reports it: we are a provider to this participant in our own right. When unsure, raise it. The Quality Manager decides under PRO-INC-02 Reportable Incidents Notification Procedure whether it is in connection with our supports and whether it is reportable, and notifies the NDIS Commission: within 24 hours of becoming aware where the incident involves the death, serious injury, abuse or neglect, unlawful sexual or physical contact or sexual misconduct of a participant, or an unauthorised restrictive practice that resulted in harm; otherwise within 5 business days. Ask the participant whether they want help to contact the Commission. With their consent, ask the other provider to confirm it has reported. If you believe a person is at serious risk, you can also phone the NDIS Commission yourself on 1800 035 544.

Result
The incident record exists, and the NDIS Commission is told in time where our supports are involved.
Record
REG-SCO-01 col AM
Time limit
Before the end of that day (our standard). For a reportable incident the law requires you to tell the Quality Manager, or the person our incident system names, as soon as possible (the Incident Rules, section 19)

Puts into action: ←Policy, commitment 4Policy C4Goes into: →Register, Linked recordsRegister col AM

Review and close

Step 29

The coordinator

If a review date arrives, or a trigger in Decision table 4 happens:

Review the Risk and Crisis Response Plan with the participant.

Start fresh. Ask what is working, what has happened and what they want now. Check each section. Update the warning signs, the call list, our hours and the providers. Rate each risk again. If the level changes, set new times from Decision table 2 the same day. After a crisis, ask what would have helped and what we got wrong. Make a new version, give the participant their copy and brief each affected provider again (step 18). For a participant at high or extreme risk, the case reviewer reads the new version. Consult the network and mainstream services (step 13) before an NDIA plan review.

Result
The plan is current, the participant has it, and the providers have been told what changed.
Record
FRM-SCO-01 Q37 to Q41; REG-SCO-01 col S; REG-SCO-01 col T
Time limit
By the time in Decision table 4, and by the date in col T (our standard)

Step 30

The coordinator

If coordination is ending, or the coordinator is changing for good:

Hand over the plan and close the row.

Follow PRO-SUP-04 Transitions to or from a Provider Procedure for notice and handover. With the participant's consent, give the next coordinator the plan, the provider list, the open actions and the report dates, before our last day. Tell each provider who the new contact is. If we must stop at short notice, the cover coordinator holds the plan until the next coordinator is confirmed. PRO-COS-01 Continuity of Supports Procedure applies. If the participant refuses handover, record it and give them their copy. Close the row only when the closing conditions in REG-SCO-01 Entry rules are all true. The Service Manager approves the closing.

Result
The participant is not left without a plan, and the row is closed correctly.
Record
REG-SCO-01 col AK; REG-SCO-01 col AL
Time limit
Before our last day of coordination (our standard)

6Decision

Decision table 1: overall risk level (step 4 for the provisional level, step 8 for the final level). Use the highest rating at Q12. Raise the level one step, to extreme at most, when Q14 shows a serious risk to someone else. At the first meeting, set a provisional level from the answers to the three safety questions.

IfThen the level is
A risk is rated extreme. Or serious harm or loss of life is likely within 4 weeks. Or a critical support is likely to stop within 14 days with nothing in placeExtreme
The highest rating is high. Or three or more risks rated medium make each other worseHigh
The highest rating is medium, and no critical support is at riskMedium
Every risk is lowLow. Tell the participant and the Service Manager within 2 business days. Use the Medium times. The participant and the Service Manager decide together whether this support fits. Any change to funding is the NDIA's decision, through a plan review the participant asks for

Decision table 2: times for each level (steps 1, 4, 8 to 12, 20, 21 and 29). Plan times count from the date of the first meeting, the second date in col C. The provisional level set at step 4 starts the clock; the final level set at step 8 can shorten the remaining time but never lengthen it. The interim safety steps at step 4 are always agreed at the first meeting.

7If it goes wrong

IfThen
The participant does not want an assessment or a plan, or refuses part of itRespect it. Explain what the plan does and what happens without it. Agree the smallest version they accept: the safety questions at Q7 to Q9 and the call list at Q26. Write "chose not to say" at Q39. Tell the Service Manager within 2 business days. Ask again at the next contact. Saying no is not a reason to end coordination
The participant does not want a person told, such as a family memberRecord it at Q6 and do not share. The only exceptions are a call to 000, a duty the law gives us, and a serious threat to life, health or safety when you cannot ask first. Tell the participant if you did
The participant cannot take part directlyAsk the people who know them well and whom they trust, with their consent where they can give it. Use what they are known to choose. A guardian or nominee decides only what their appointment covers. The coordinator never decides for the participant
You cannot reach a participant at high or extreme riskExtreme risk: try twice that day, in two different ways, then phone the person at Q9 or the first number at Q26 the same day. If there is still no contact by the end of that day, do what the participant said at Q30: call or send the person or service they named, and ask police for a welfare check only if they agreed to it or the plan is silent. High risk: the same steps, finished by the end of the next business day. Where there is an immediate risk to life, call 000 whatever the plan says. Never contact a person named at Q6. Tell the Service Manager the same day, and the case reviewer for a sole trader. Write every try with its time at col AC
You cannot reach a participant at medium or low riskTry three times in 10 business days, in two ways. Write each try. Tell the Service Manager at the end of that time. Keep the plan open and try again at the next interval
The coordinator is away, sick or cannot be reachedThe cover coordinator takes over the same business day and reads the plan if they have not. The Service Manager tells the participant who to contact. For a sole trader, the cover coordinator is the coordinator from another provider named on adoption. If no cover can be reached, the Service Manager or the Chief Executive acts, and phones each participant at high or extreme risk that day
A provider will not engage, or has not confirmed after 10 business daysThe Service Manager phones their manager. Tell the participant. Offer the next choice from step 15. If their response puts the participant at risk, raise it as an incident (step 28) or a complaint under PRO-FBK-01
A provider gives short notice to stop, or a worker does not arriveGo to step 26. Phone the provider, then the next choice at Q32. Tell the participant what is happening. PRO-COS-01 Continuity of Supports Procedure applies
The plan is within 12 weeks of its reassessment date and no review has been scheduledAsk the NDIA in writing, with the participant's agreement, to confirm the reassessment date. Tell the participant that the plan stays in effect until a new plan starts. Tell the Service Manager. If supports are at risk, go to step 26
A report deadline will be missedTell the recipient before the date passes and give a new date. Tell the Service Manager the same day. Write the reason at col AH. The Quality Manager tells the Chief Executive of any report more than 10 business days late
Coordination hours or funding will run out before the plan endsTell the participant and the Service Manager within 5 business days of the check. Agree priorities with the participant. They may ask the NDIA for a plan review. Do not stop contact with a participant at extreme risk without a handover under step 30. The Chief Executive decides what unfunded contact we can carry and for how long; ask the NDIA for a plan variation the same day
The participant chooses a risk you are worried aboutDo not stop them and do not withdraw. Explain the risk and the options in a way they understand. Complete FRM-RGT-04 Dignity of Risk Decision Record for a risk rated high or extreme. Tell the Service Manager the same day
Someone asks for a restraint, a lock, a withheld item or a medicine to calm to be written into the planDo not write it in and do not carry it out. Tell the Service Manager the same day. PRO-BSP-02 Regulated Restrictive Practices Procedure applies. If one has been used, raise an incident report (step 28)
The participant tells you about harm, or you see signs of itMake them safe. Follow PRO-SGD-01 Violence, Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation and Discrimination Procedure and PRO-INC-01 Incident Management Procedure that day. Planning waits until they are ready
You are not trained or signed off for the participant's risksTell the Service Manager before you take the case, or the day you see it. They give the case to a signed-off coordinator, or arrange advice and supervision. You do not carry on alone
Your concern is about a colleague, the Service Manager or the Chief ExecutiveTell the Service Manager. If it is about them, tell the Chief Executive. If it is about the Chief Executive, tell the chair of the governing body. In a provider with one owner, tell the independent contact for concerns. You can phone the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544. POL-GOV-03 Whistleblower and Disclosure Protection Policy protects you
The system is down and you cannot open the planUse the participant's own copy of Section E to read the call list. Phone the Service Manager, who holds a copy of the call lists for participants at high or extreme risk. Enter what happened in col AE within 1 business day of the system coming back

8Done means

Coordination is in place for a participant when all of these are true:

  • the participant has a plan they helped make, agreed or with their disagreement recorded, and have their copy in the form they chose
  • the case reviewer has signed the plan, for a participant at high or extreme risk
  • the cover coordinator has read the plan
  • every provider is briefed and has confirmed they understand
  • the participant chose each provider from checked options, and directed how their funds are used
  • every report and date is listed, and each due date is diarised.

These records now exist:

  • the Risk and Crisis Response Plan (FRM-SCO-01), with its sign-off, on the participant's file
  • the consent record (FRM-INF-01) for each person we may talk to
  • the participant's row in REG-SCO-01, with columns A to AM filled as far as the stage reached
  • the options and choice record (FRM-SCO-02) for each support, with its row in REG-SCO-01 sheet 2
  • for any event, an entry in col AE, and an incident report (FRM-INC-01) where it applies
  • after each plan review, a new version of FRM-SCO-01 and a new date in col T
  • at the end, a closed row with its handover record.

9Quick card

150 words

  • Open the participant's plan and follow the first steps for this kind of crisis (step 26)
  • Phone the people on the call list, in order, until someone takes responsibility (step 26)

  • Cannot reach a participant at high or extreme risk: try twice in two ways, ring their contact, then follow Q30 of their plan on a welfare check (If it goes wrong)
  • Brief every provider before their first support, and get their confirmation (step 18)
  • Give the participant their copy of the plan the day it is agreed (step 12)
  • Check the budget and the dates in the first 5 business days of every month (step 22)
  • Send each report by its due date, or tell the recipient before it passes (step 24)

form.intro:
Use this form to make a with a participant who receives from [Provider name]. The plan names the participant's risks, their warning signs, what helps, and who does what if a crisis or a breakdown of their supports happens.

The coordinator makes it with the participant. The participant leads. Their own words go in Sections B, C and E wherever they can.

  • Section A: complete at the first meeting. It holds the three safety questions and who we may talk to.
  • Sections B to E: complete with the participant after the first meeting, inside the time set for their risk level in PRO-SCO-02 Decision table 2, counted from the first meeting. For a participant at extreme risk, Section A and the call list at questions 25 and 26 form the interim plan, made within 1 business day of the first meeting; Sections B to E follow within 5 business days. Two or three sittings is normal.
  • Section F: this is our own record of how we checked each provider. It is not part of the plan we share. The participant can ask to see it at any time.
  • Section G: complete when the plan is agreed. The case reviewer signs before the plan is issued for a participant at high or extreme risk, and within 10 business days of issue for every other participant.

We share Sections C and E, and the parts of Section D the participant agrees, with providers. With the participant's agreement we also share the risk factors at questions 11 and 14 that a provider needs for their part. Never share questions 5 and 6, the history at question 12, or Section F. The participant's and providers' copies omit those parts (question 40).

Have ready:

  • the participant's NDIS plan
  • their communication preferences (FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form)
  • the consent record (FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form)
  • what the participant wants to be called.

What happens next: the coordinator gives the participant their copy, enters the answers marked for REG-SCO-01 Support Coordination Register, and briefs each provider under PRO-SCO-02.

When systems are down, use a paper copy. Enter it in the system within 1 business day of the system coming back (our standard). Never leave a paper copy in a car.
form.privacy:
We collect this information to keep you safe, to plan for a crisis and to coordinate your supports. We collect it from you first, and from other people only if you agree.

We share the plan only with the people you choose, and only the parts you agree. We will share without your agreement only to call 000 or to meet a legal duty. We will also share to stop a serious threat to someone's life, health or safety. We do this only when we cannot ask you first. We tell you if we do.

Your coordinator, their cover coordinator, the Service Manager and the case reviewer read the whole form. The Quality Manager and an approved quality auditor may see it at an audit, unless you have said no. We keep it for 7 years after we stop coordinating your supports, or longer where the NDIS Act 2013 (section 45B) or the law of [state or territory] requires.

You can ask to see what we hold, and ask us to correct it. To complain about how we handle your information, contact [role and contact]. POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets how we store and protect it.
form.after:
• Coordinator: enter the answers marked for REG-SCO-01 in the register within 1 business day (our standard). The row is opened first under PRO-SCO-02 step 2.
  • Coordinator: give the participant their copy, in the format they chose, on the day it is agreed (our standard).
  • Cover coordinator: read the plan within 2 business days of issue, the same day for a participant at extreme risk (our standard).
  • Coordinator: brief each provider on the parts the participant agreed to share, before the provider's first support, under PRO-SCO-02 step 18.
  • Service Manager: read each plan for a participant at high or extreme risk within 1 business day of the case reviewer's sign-off (our standard). Read every other plan at the monthly read of REG-SCO-01.
  • The completed form is filed on the participant's file. Keep it for 7 years after the row in REG-SCO-01 is closed (our standard), or longer where section 45B of the NDIS Act 2013 or the law of [state or territory] requires. Where the participant was under 18, keep it until they turn 25 when that is later.

register.proves:
This register is the running record of at [Provider name]. Sheet 1 holds one row for each for each period. A row shows the participant's risks, their plan, the engaged, what we checked and what we reported, and when. Sheet 2 holds one row for each FRM-SCO-02 Support Options and Choice Record: each decision about a support, skills plan, monthly funds check, support review and plan review preparation.

Short names used here:

  • "The Registration Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Provider Registration and Practice Standards) Rules 2018.
  • "The Incident Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Incident Management and Reportable Incidents) Rules 2018.
  • "The Code" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Code of Conduct) Rules 2018, section 6.
  • "The " means the National Disability Insurance Agency. The Quality Indicators call it "the Agency".

What it evidences, and how long it is kept:

  • Indicators evidenced: s 64 (1) to s 64 (6), on sheet 1. Sheet 2 holds the record for s 65 (1) to s 65 (4). FRM-SCO-02 Support Options and Choice Record and PRO-SCO-03 Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure feed sheet 2.
  • Legal basis: Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 6, clause 3, and Quality Indicators Guidelines, section 64. The Rules do not set the columns of this register. The columns are our standard, built from the six indicators.
  • Records that are kept elsewhere stay there. An incident is recorded in REG-INC-01 Incident Register, and a complaint in REG-FBK-01 Complaints Register. This register holds the number of each, in column AM.
  • Retention: keep each row for 7 years after the row is closed (our standard), and in every case for the 7 years that section 45B of the NDIS Act 2013 (from 27 August 2026) requires for records of claims and supports. For a participant who was under 18 when coordination started, keep it until they turn 25, when that is later (our standard).
  • Other law can require longer. Check the law of [state or territory] before any row is destroyed. Never destroy a row while a claim, an inquiry, a complaint or an investigation is open.

Every column is filled for every row, except where the Required column says otherwise.
register.entry:
1. The opens the row within 1 of the participant agreeing to start (our standard). When the coordinator is away, the or the Service Manager opens it.
  2. Keep one open row for each participant. When a new NDIS plan starts, the coordinator closes the old row with the reason "plan period ended and a new row opened" and opens a new one within 10 business days of learning the new plan dates (our standard). Column AM links the two rows. The plan and risk level carry over by copy and are then reviewed. No handover is needed for this kind of closing.
  3. Add each entry on the day it happens, or within 1 business day (our standard). Where a column holds more than one entry, each entry is a dated line with the name of the person who made it. A new line never replaces an old one.
  4. Never overwrite or delete an entry. A correction is a new version of the row, with the date, your name and the reason. Where the register is a workbook, keep version history switched on.
  5. For a crisis, write the time we learned of it and the time of our first response in column AE. The two times show whether we met the 2 hour standard.
  6. Long text stays in the form. Where a column says "one dated line each", the lines live on a child sheet keyed by column A (see Rows), and the participant's row shows the latest date and the next due date. In a workbook, write one line and the question number, for example "see FRM-SCO-01 Q12". Never copy a participant's full account into a cell.
  7. Column K is filled at the first meeting. Columns O, Q and S are filled inside the time in PRO-SCO-02 Decision table 2. For a participant at high or extreme risk, columns K, Q and S are filled before any provider is briefed.
  8. When systems are down, write the entry on paper and enter it within 1 business day of the system coming back.
  9. When a row is about a concern with a coordinator, the Service Manager restricts who can see it. When the concern is about the Service Manager, the Chief Executive does. In a provider with one owner, the does.
  10. Reopen a closed row when new information arrives. Set column AJ to "open" and record the reason in column AM.

A row is closed only when all of these are true:

  • the reason for closing is recorded in column AK
  • every report in column AG up to the closing date is sent, or the reason it was not sent is in column AH
  • every event in column AE has a plan review date
  • the plan was handed over, or the participant's refusal of handover is recorded in column AL; or the reason in column AK is "plan period ended and a new row opened" and column AM links the rows, in which case no handover is needed
  • the participant has their copy of the current plan, recorded in column S
  • the Service Manager has approved the closing. For a participant who was at high or extreme risk, the has also read the row.

The review log is a sheet in the register workbook or system. Each line holds the date, the reviewer's name, the kind of review, the rows read, what was found and what was sent on.

A sole trader reads the register every week, and writes the monthly and 3 monthly review in one sitting at least every month. The case reviewer, the person outside the business named on adoption, does the reads in the table above for the case reviewer and, every 3 months, reads every row in column AE and every row on sheet 2. The independent contact for concerns, named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register, receives concerns only, and may be the same person as the case reviewer.

Two events of the same kind for different participants in 3 months is a trend. The Quality Manager checks whether the plan template, a provider or our training must change.

The Quality Manager gives the NDIS Commission any information or document from this register that it asks for. They give it within the time the Commission sets (NDIS Act 2013, section 73F(2)(i)), which is at least 14 days unless the Commissioner shortens it for a risk of serious harm (section 73F(3)).
register.see:
• The coordinator and the cover coordinator can see their participants' rows.
  • The Service Manager, the Quality Manager and the Chief Executive can see every row.
  • The case reviewer can see the rows they review.
  • A participant can ask to see their own row. We remove other people's details first.
  • A provider cannot see this register. A provider sees only the parts of the plan the participant agreed to share (column N).
  • Column N hides the reason a person must not be told. That reason stays in the plan, with the participant.
  • An approved quality auditor sees a participant's row at an audit unless the participant has said no. The NDIS Commission and police see rows as the law allows or requires.
  • A lawyer or adviser acting for [Provider name] sees only the rows needed for that advice.

Rows hold sensitive personal and health information, and sometimes information about people at risk from someone close to them. Keep the register in [system name], with a login for each person and a log of changes. Lock away any paper record. Never leave one in a participant's home or in a car. POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets the wider privacy rules.
register.rows: The rows are the data. They are kept in the workbook or system built to this specification, not in this document. Sheet 1 holds one row per participant per plan period. Where a column on sheet 1 says "one dated line each" (columns W, X, AA, AB, AC, AD, AE, AF and AH), the workbook holds those lines on a child sheet keyed by column A, with one row per consultation, provider, briefing, meeting, contact, delivery check, event, funds check or report; the participant's row shows the latest date and the next due date. Sheet 2 holds one row per FRM-SCO-02 copy, with the columns marked "Sheet 2" above.
